questions.stem: How is Data Quality defined in one line?
options: When data is stored in the Cloud
When we compare data against Business Rules
When data has a primary key
When data is loaded on time
questions.explanation: 'Data Quality is when we compare data against Business Rules.'

questions.stem: How many dimensions of Data Quality are described?
questions.explanation: The six dimensions are Accuracy, Completeness, Consistency, Validity, Uniqueness and Timeliness.

questions.stem: On what does the Accuracy dimension of Data Quality depend?
options: The number of rows in a table
questions.explanation: Accuracy depends on traceability through data lineage; without lineage, accuracy is always questionable.

questions.stem: What does Completeness mean as a Data Quality dimension?
options: Having every possible piece of data
Having data in a consistent format
Ensuring critical attributes exist to fulfil KPIs or regulatory needs
questions.explanation: Completeness is not about all data but about ensuring the critical attributes exist to serve the business purpose, KPIs or regulatory needs.

questions.stem: A customer's birthdate appearing in three different formats across platforms is a failure of which dimension?
questions.explanation: Consistency means data values must not conflict across systems; a birthdate in three formats collapses trust.

questions.stem: Which dimension is violated by duplicate customer IDs or accounts?
questions.explanation: Uniqueness requires records to be free of duplication; duplicate IDs lead to wasted marketing spend and skewed analytics.

questions.stem: What is the difference between Data Quality and Data Quality Management (DQM)?
options: DQM is only for cloud data
DQM is the state; Data Quality is the discipline
Data Quality applies to structured data; DQM to unstructured
Data Quality is the state; DQM is the discipline of processes and controls that achieve and sustain it
questions.explanation: Data Quality is the state in which data exhibits the six dimensions; DQM is the discipline of processes and controls needed to reach and keep that state.

questions.stem: Which method to improve Data Quality identifies and merges duplicate records?
questions.explanation: Matching and Linking identifies and merges duplicate records; profiling detects anomalies and geocoding enriches location data.

questions.stem: What is the correct order of the Data Quality Life Cycle?
questions.explanation: The life cycle runs Detect, Investigate, Analyse, Correct (as close to the source as possible) and Sustain.

questions.stem: Which statement about the cost of poor Data Quality is made?
options: Bad data costs more than no data at all
Bad data is always better than no data
Bad data has no cost if it is stored cheaply
Poor data quality only affects reports
Poor data quality cannot lead to regulatory fines
questions.explanation: Poor data quality is linked to fines, reputational loss, failed AI models and operational costs; simply put, bad data costs more than no data at all.
